name: Liberty Bell, Concord and Lexington Towers

legs.connect: Drop from the Liberty Bell summit to the notch between the two spires, then climb the neighbouring tower from there.
Rappel from the top of Concord into the next notch to the east, then follow the ridge crest to Lexington's summit.

how: Three neighbouring granite spires are strung along one ridge and are linked in a single day by going west to east. Start on the most popular route of the group, cross the first notch, and climb the second tower by its three-pitch north side, around 5.7 and somewhat loose-looking. A short rappel puts you in the next notch for the third tower, whose last pitch is mostly easy ridge scrambling. The link adds route-finding in the notches and a couple of rappels over doing the climbs separately.
descent: From the last tower, scramble down the ridge to the top of the second pitch, then rappel the route twice to the packs left at the base. Walk back down the approach trail to the highway.
logistics: Leave packs at the base of the last tower or carry only what the day needs. The notches fill with parties on summer weekends, so a weekday start before dawn avoids waits at the rappels. Snow-free from midsummer through early fall.
notes: Concord to Lexington alone is a commonly done short link-up. Liberty Bell was not climbed in the second page's report. Liberty-Concord descent into the notch is not described in detail in either page. 5.7 grades for both north faces come from the second page. The full Liberty group traverse also adds the Early Winters Spires (not verified here).

name: Golden Horn, Tower Mountain and Mount Hardy

legs.route: Snowy Lakes route from Upper Snowy Lake

legs.connect: Walk back toward Lower Snowy Lake and pick up the climbers' path across talus to the big gully below the summit.

legs.route: Via Methow Pass, climbers' path along the ridge
legs.connect: Return to the Snowy Lakes trail, rejoin the Pacific Crest Trail toward Methow Pass and leave it on the climbers' path. Overnight gear can stay at the pass while you climb.

how: Camp at Upper Snowy Lake, which is close to both of the first two peaks. Golden Horn is a long scramble to a notch, then an awkward wrap-around to a summit block with a short mantle that some parties protect with a rope. Tower is a continuous class 3 gully, then a short exposed move to the ridge. Hardy is non-technical but loose and lies on the way back along the Pacific Crest Trail. Two peaks from the lake is the common outing; adding Hardy makes the exit a very long day.
descent: Golden Horn needs a short rappel, about 40 feet with a 30 metre rope, then retrace to the notch. Tower and Hardy are descended by their ascent routes. From Methow Pass the Pacific Crest Trail leads about 11 miles south to Rainy Pass.
logistics: Start at Rainy Pass on the Pacific Crest Trail (about 10 miles to the lake junction) or from Swamp Creek on the highway for a shorter, steeper way in to Hardy. A 30 metre rope and a few small rock pieces are enough. Snow-free late July to September.
notes: All three peaks together appear in one page (35-mile, two-day trip); Hardy with Golden Horn from Methow Pass is a second page (ski trip, winter conditions); Golden Horn plus Tower from Upper Snowy Lake is a third (which added Azurite the next day). Golden Horn summit class ranges from 3 to low 5th across sources.

name: Azurite Peak and Mount Ballard

legs.connect: Break camp after Azurite and continue past Azurite Pass down the Mill Creek drainage to a camp below Ballard, then climb to its ridge next morning.

how: Both peaks are reached from the Azurite Pass area and have been linked on one trip by crossing the pass and descending the neighbouring creek. Azurite is a class 3 route with a class 4 section on its west rib. Ballard is class 3-4 with loose rock, a notch and gendarme on the south ridge, and a low fifth class step on the summit block. Expect snow travel in spring and a faint, brushy trail.
descent: Descend each peak by its ascent route. After Ballard, one party followed the creek out to the Canyon Creek trail and highway through heavy brush, which was the hardest part of their trip.
logistics: Approach from the highway at Swamp Creek via Snowy Lakes, or by the Methow River trail to the Pacific Crest Trail. The old mine area was closed for mine clean-up when one party passed through, so check the current status before choosing the loop.
notes: Only one page reports completing both; a second climber planned the traverse to Ballard from Azurite and turned back for weather. Mill Creek trail is nearly absent per the first page. DROPPED by reviewer: only one completed report.
